description: Stereo ping-pong delay modelled on an analogue bucket-brigade pedal, with the size of the bucket line, the filters around it and the compander all brought out as controls

params.text: Sets the delay time; the span depends on the Stages setting, running from a hundredth of the longest time to all of it
Sets how much of the output goes back into the input, 0 to 3; it passes unity well before the top, and the module will self-oscillate up there
Tap a tempo: two presses set the delay time to the gap between them
Sets the cutoff of the filters either side of the bucket line, 200Hz at fully counter-clockwise to 10kHz at fully clockwise, which makes the repeats brighter or darker
Sets the resonance of those same filters, 0 to 1, which changes the character of the repeats most at high feedback
Sets how much noise the bucket line adds, 0 to 1; more noise makes self-oscillation start sooner
Sets how many buckets the delay line has, 256 to 16384 in powers of two; fewer gives very short delays for chorus, more gives longer and brighter delays
Sets how steep the filters either side of the bucket line are, 6dB per octave to 24dB per octave; steeper is cleaner and duller, shallower is dirtier and brighter
Sets how quickly the compander reacts, 0.1Hz to 40Hz; a low setting gives the repeats a slight fade in and out
Sets the level going into the delay, 0 to 4; the dry path is not touched by it, and a lamp lights when the delay circuit is overloaded
Spreads the two repeats apart, 0 for both channels the same and 1 for full ping-pong; with Inv R on it does nothing
Makes the right repeat the inverted left repeat, which with a small Stages setting, no feedback and a moving delay time gives a chorus
Crossfades between dry and wet, both at full level at the centre

inputs.text: Added to the Time knob at a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, the total clamped to the knob's own range
Added to the Feedback knob at three tenths per volt
The left audio input, or the whole signal when it is the only cable
The right audio input; with no cable it takes the left input

outputs.text: The left dry and wet signals mixed at the Mix setting
The right dry and wet signals mixed at the Mix setting

notes: the delay time span moves with the Stages setting, so changing the number of buckets changes what the Time knob reaches as well as the tone
the feedback knob goes to 300%, which is far past unity; the output is held to -10V and 10V but the delay line will sing on its own well below the top of the travel
both inputs sum all channels of a polyphonic cable to one, and both outputs are monophonic
the lamp in the Tap button blinks at the current delay time

inputs.0:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
inputs.1:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
